title: Instruction-file approval cards render attacker-sized full content with no per-card or aggregate cap, polled every 2 s
description: A prompt-injected sandbox agent can queue up to PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX=20 pending instruction-file write approvals per sandbox, each carrying up to max_write_bytes=1 MiB of agent-chosen content (write_file 'content' is exempt from TOOL_ARG_MAX). The approval UI renders every pending card's content in full through autoescape + _shown (escape_controls), with no truncation and no aggregate cap, and the index approvals fragment aggregates the pending set of every sandbox. Measured locally with the real web filters: 20 cards x 1 MiB of control-byte content rendered in 10.11 s and produced an 80 MiB response body. index.html:25 re-polls /ui/approvals every 2 s and web.render builds and SHA-256-hashes the full body even to return a 204, so the cost is paid on every poll and multiplied by the number of sandboxes. The human approval view becomes unusable and control-plane threadpool workers are tied up while the human is trying to triage the attacker's pending writes.
root_cause: _approvals.html:13 renders a.args.content in full with no length bound; escape_controls expands each control character about 4x; there is no per-card content cap and no aggregate rendered-bytes cap on the approvals fragment; web.render always materialises and hashes the whole body even when it will return 204; write_file content bypasses TOOL_ARG_MAX so one card can be 1 MiB, with 20 pending per sandbox, and the index fragment aggregates all sandboxes.
intended_behavior: The approvals view, polled every 2 s on the index and sandbox pages, must bound the CPU and bytes a single poll costs so that attacker-chosen pending content cannot make each poll cost seconds of control-plane CPU or tens of MiB of response.

trace.description: The TOOL_ARG_MAX check excludes the 'content' key, so write_file content is bounded only by max_write_bytes (1 MiB).
approvals.create stores the full args (including 1 MiB content); up to PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX=20 rows can be pending per sandbox.
Lists every pending approval; with sandbox_id=None (the index poll) it aggregates all sandboxes into one fragment.
Builds the entire response body and hashes it on every request, even when it returns 204.

renders the full content through _shown; no truncation or aggregate cap.

evidence.description: max_write_bytes = 1024 * 1024, the only bound on write_file content size.
Local measurement: 20 x 1 MiB control-byte cards render in 10.110 s producing an 80.0 MiB body using the real web filters and _approvals.html.

conditions.description: Attacker holds a per-sandbox agent token (the assumed prompt-injected agent).
A human has an approvals view open; the index and sandbox pages poll /ui/approvals every 2 s automatically.
Up to 20 pending instruction-file write approvals per sandbox, each about 1 MiB of control-byte content.

execution.attacker_perspective: As the sandbox agent, fill the per-sandbox pending queue with maximum-size instruction-file writes; every human poll of the approvals view then re-renders them.
payloads: repeat 20 times with different instruction-file paths to reach PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX
instructions: In the sandbox, build a Jinja2 environment for agentbox/templates with autoescape on, finalize=agentbox.web._shown, and filters oneline/short as in web.register.
Construct 20 pending-approval dicts with tool='write_file', preview.instruction_file set, and args.content = '\x01' * (1024*1024).
Render _approvals.html once and record render time and body size.
execution.observed_result: Rendering 20 pending cards x 1 MiB control-byte content took 10.110 s and produced an 80.0 MiB (83,909,242 byte) body.

remediation.strategy: Show only a capped prefix of instruction-file content in the 2 s-polled list, with a separate non-polled 'view full content' page for the approval being inspected; cap aggregate rendered bytes per fragment; avoid rebuilding and rehashing an unchanged large fragment on every poll.

likelihood.reason: Triggered by a prompt-injected agent under default configuration; the UI polls automatically.

impact.reason: Degrades or denies the human approval UI and ties up control-plane threadpool workers while the human triages the attacker's writes; no data loss or privilege change.

confidence.reason: Measured locally with the real web filters and template; bounds and per-poll rebuild are source-confirmed.
